en.title: Use attribution models without false certainty
en.summary: Treat attribution as a structured way to learn about contribution, not a machine for assigning perfect credit.

blocks.heading: Key takeaways
items: Every attribution model makes a useful simplification.
Pair model outputs with experiments, customer evidence, and commercial context.

blocks.heading: Credit is not causation
paragraphs: A model can show where recorded touchpoints appear in a path. It cannot, on its own, prove that each touchpoint caused the outcome.
Use model differences as questions for investigation rather than proof that one channel deserves all the budget.

blocks.heading: Choose a model for the decision
paragraphs: Select the simplest model that helps the team make a specific allocation or measurement decision. Explain its blind spots before presenting the result.
Revisit the model when the buying cycle, tracking coverage, or channel mix changes materially.

blocks.heading: Editorial view
blocks.body: Attribution is most valuable when it makes uncertainty discussable and the next test more precise.
